name: Question 3
worked_solution:
From the vector addition rule, we have

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}[f(t)-g(t)]\,\text{d}t={\int }_{0}^{1}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{0}^{1}g(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[f(t)-g(t)]\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{0}^{1}g(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2},\,2,\,1⟩-⟨1,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2},\,1,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Calculate ∫01[f(t)−g(t)]dt given that ∫01f(t)dt=⟨12,2,1⟩ and ∫01g(t)dt=⟨1,1,1⟩.

a
⟨12,−1,0⟩
b
⟨−12,−12,2⟩
c
⟨−12,1,0⟩
d
⟨12,1,0⟩
e
⟨−12,12,2⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the vector addition rule, we have

∫01[f(t)−g(t)]dt=∫01f(t)dt−∫01g(t)dt.

Therefore,

∫01[f(t)−g(t)]dt=∫01f(t)dt−∫01g(t)dt=⟨12,2,1⟩−⟨1,1,1⟩=⟨−12,1,0⟩.
